provenance.derivation: Composed in the manner of kasane no irome, for winter: 4 of our own published entries read as layers from the outermost inward — 薄霜 usu-shimo, then 冬杉 fuyu-sugi, then 冬影 fuyu-kage, then 霜夜 shimo-yo. NOT a historical combination: no layer is asserted to reproduce a documented Heian kasane, and no value was read from any kasane table. Chosen by hand, not generated. Every adjacent pair of layers is more than ΔE00 5 apart — the distance below which the product calls two items the same (FR-44) — because a layering whose edges cannot be told apart is not one; gate 11 recomputes that under the current engine on every run, so no figure is typed here. Weights fall inward (1, 0.8, 0.6, 0.5) because each inner layer shows less than the one over it.
provenance.editorialNotes: Frost over evergreen, read outermost first: a thin-frost white (薄霜) over a winter cedar green (冬杉), then a violet winter shadow (冬影), and a frost-night blue-black (霜夜) as the innermost edge. The green and the violet shadow are the only layers with colour in them, the green the stronger; the rest is frost and night, which is how an evergreen reads in winter. The name is ours (霜杉, "Frosted Cedar"), coined as a seasonal image the way the historical names are; it is not presented as a traditional kasane name.
